findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/RootsOfUnity/PrimitiveRoots.lean:444 `theorem geom_sum_eq_zero [IsDomain R] {ζ : R} (hζ : IsPrimitiveRoot ζ k) (hk : 1 < k) : ∑ i ∈ range k, ζ ^ i = 0`; `Cyclotomic.isPrimitiveRoot_complexRoot` at Basic.lean:468 supplies `hζ` for any `e` with `NeZero e`.
findings.fix: Drop the `3`-specific lemma; either state `geom_sum_complexRoot_eq_zero (he : 1 < e) : ∑ i ∈ Finset.range e, complexRoot e ^ i = 0 := isPrimitiveRoot_complexRoot.geom_sum_eq_zero he`, or apply Mathlib's lemma directly in `CyclicThree.lean` and specialize with `Finset.sum_range_succ`.
findings.issue: `complexRoot_three_sq_add_self_add_one_eq_zero` hardcodes `e = 3` in a file whose every other `complexRoot` lemma (`star_complexRoot`, `star_complexRoot_eq_pow`, `eval₂_cyclotomic_complexRoot`) is general in `e`. The general statement is `∑ i ∈ Finset.range e, complexRoot e ^ i = 0` for `1 < e`.

findings.evidence: Same file, Implementation notes (lines 56-60): "The general results are stated over an arbitrary finite coefficient field `F` with the splitting of the centre as an explicit hypothesis, rather than over `ZMod p` with a good Dixon prime"; `card_centralCharacterSearch` (line 124) is general-F and `card_centralCharacterSearch_of_isGoodDixonPrime` (line 145) is its derived special case.
findings.fix: Take `{S : Type*} [DecidableEq S] (f : R → S)` and drop the `p` argument; state the exhaustion lemma over the file's general `F` with the splitting hypothesis `h : Nonempty (Subalgebra.center F (MonoidAlgebra F G) ≃ₐ[F] (ConjClasses G → F))` using `card_centralCharacterSearch h`, and derive the good-prime version from it as the existing `card_*` pair already does.
findings.issue: `modularCentralRows p f M` fixes the codomain to `ZMod p` although its body (`Finset.univ.image fun i j => f (M i j)`) uses nothing about `ZMod p`, and the explicit `p` is already determined by the type of `f`, so every call site repeats it (`modularCentralRows 5 (fun x : ℤ => (x : ZMod 5)) M` in Rational/Dihedral/Four.lean:124). Relatedly, `centralCharacterSearch_eq_modularCentralRows_of_isGoodDixonPrime` at line 152 is stated only over `ZMod p` at a good prime, but its proof uses good-primeness solely via `card_centralCharacterSearch_of_isGoodDixonPrime`.

findings.evidence: EigenvectorSearch.lean:238-266 — the body and both lemmas are pure `Matrix.map`/`Matrix.submatrix` reindexing; uses are IntegerChecker.lean:131 and CyclicThree.lean:267.
findings.fix: Generalize to `{R S : Type*} (f : R → S) (table : Matrix (Fin d.numClasses) (Fin d.numClasses) R) : Matrix (Fin (Nat.card (ConjClasses G))) (ConjClasses G) S` (adjusting the name accordingly); the two existing call sites (`complexTableOfInteger`, `cyclicGroupThreeComplexCharacterTable`) instantiate `S := ℂ` unchanged.
findings.issue: `complexTableOfMap` generalizes the entry map but leaves the target fixed at `ℂ`; neither the definition (`(table.map f).submatrix _ _`) nor `complexTableOfMap_apply`/`complexTableOfMap_apply_classOf` uses any `ℂ` structure. This blocks reuse for the exact `Cyclotomic e`-valued table the cyclotomic checker path will need.

summary: Three half-generalizations: a hardcoded cube-root identity added to the otherwise e-general cyclotomic file when the general geometric-sum form is one line from Mathlib, and two newly refactored ClassData definitions whose coefficient targets (ZMod p, C) are pinned although nothing in the definitions or proofs uses them.
